**Finding submitted: deviation (AUDIT).**

- **What we found:** The agreement contains no audit clause as such (no "audit", "inspect", or "verify" language anywhere). The only Customer-facing verification right is § 11.3, where "IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b)" and may then act "in its sole and reasonable discretion." The § 11.2(b) AUP warranty and IBM's unilateral right to amend the AUP (§ 13.2) make this a live, recurring exposure.
- **Why it fails the fallback:** No frequency cap, no prior notice of the investigation itself (the p0137 notice is best-efforts only and triggers only before access restriction or content removal), no cost allocation, and no limit on access to our systems or premises — i.e. unlimited/unannounced inspection, which the playbook treats as walk-away.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** Inserted a limiting paragraph after p0137 — once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, our business hours, at IBM's expense, by IBM or an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and no access (including remote access) to our systems, networks or premises — with a narrow carve-out where IBM reasonably believes a violation is ongoing and poses imminent harm, preserving IBM's emergency remedies in 11.3(a)–(d).
- **Noted, not flagged:** No underpayment-based cost-shifting trigger was added, since this right concerns AUP compliance rather than usage-based charges. 15 days' notice is offered as a fallback in the comment.
